newsitem.title: USA: CHINA MAY HAVE BOUGHT CARGO OF U.S. SOYOIL - TRADE.
newsitem.headline: CHINA MAY HAVE BOUGHT CARGO OF U.S. SOYOIL - TRADE.

text.p: China was said to be checking soyoil freight rates, indicating it recently bought a cargo of about 20,000 to 25,000 tonnes or more of U.S. soyoil, traders and U.S. exporters said.
"There are some rumors in the freight market, but so far no confirmation," a U.S. soyoil exporter said.
Rumors circulated on the Chicago Board of Trade among soyoil traders that China on Monday night purchased a cargo of U.S. soyoil for September shipment and would buy another cargo for October.
"It may be more than that," another U.S. soyoil exporter said, referring to market talk of one cargo sold to China.

"There is probably some truth to it," he said, citing more Chinese interest for U.S. soyoil. "I think we are getting prices that are probably attractive to some people in China for a number of different products."
But other soyoil exporters doubted China had purchased a cargo of U.S. soyoil.

"I am sure that a vessel will leave the U.S. Gulf in September to China but it happens about every month and it is small lots of corn oil, sunoil and refined products," a third U.S. soyoil exporter said. "It does not all go to China, some of it goes to (South) Korea."
As for a full cargo heading for China, "The answer is I have not heard about it, don't know about it and doubt it very much," this exporter said.
